# IRGC threatens countries aiding US, says Hormuz will remain closed



Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guards threatened countries assisting the United States with a “harsh response” unless they changed their conduct, according to a statement issued on Thursday.

The IRGC said the Strait of Hormuz would remain closed as long as the US continued making threats and intervening in maritime movements in the region.

It said two oil tankers attempted to leave through what it called an unsafe route south of the strait on Wednesday night under the direction of US aircraft. Both vessels turned back after a major fire broke out aboard one of them, the IRGC said, without providing evidence.

The Guards also said Iran controlled the Strait of Hormuz and vowed to “punish the aggressor” later on Thursday.

Iran's ballistic missile strike on US forces in Jordan and its seizure of three oil tankers in the Strait of Hormuz have dealt a fresh blow to efforts to preserve last month's Iran-US understanding.

After Iran fired several ballistic missiles toward a US military base in Jordan early Wednesday Tehran time, US President Donald Trump vowed to hit back hard.

Hours later, the naval arm of Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) announced it had struck and detained three "offending" oil tankers in the Strait of Hormuz.

Several analysts said the combination of the Jordan strike and Tehran's actions in the Strait of Hormuz suggested Iran was no longer content to react to US pressure but was instead trying to seize the initiative and reshape the course of the confrontation.

Political analyst Ruhollah Rahimpour told Iran International the overnight missile launches and the Hormuz operation reflected a deliberate strategy of escalation.

## Tehran is stalling as Washington wavers. And Israel is watching the Hormuz drama eclipse the real fight: stopping a nuclear Iran.

By[MAJ.-GEN. (RET.) AMOS YADLIN](/author/maj-gen-ret-amos-yadlin)

Updated:

Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s [visit to Washington](https://www.jpost.com/israel-news/article-904064) yesterday stood out primarily for what it lacked: a joint press statement and a photo op alongside US President Donald Trump. These images are particularly crucial for Netanyahu ahead of the elections in Israel, but their absence also reflects the growing sensitivity in the White House toward Israeli attempts to influence its policy on Iran.

The meeting took place against the backdrop of the de facto ceasefire between Iran and the United States. # Trump is stuck in Iran. Here’s one idea that could offer a way out

![Stephen Collinson](https://media.cnn.com/api/v1/images/stellar/prod/stephen-collinson-0002.jpg?c=16x9&q=h_270,w_480,c_fill/c_thumb,g_face,w_50,h_50)

The US war in Iran is in desperate need of new thinking.

Despite [new US strikes Wednesday](https://www.cnn.com/2026/07/29/world/live-news/iran-trump-news#cms6rvx3k00003d6a4topfhhu) following President Donald Trump’s f-bomb warning that Iran is due another “beating,” he has yet to show he can blast Tehran back to talks.

But diplomacy that he hailed as bringing historic peace to the Middle East also failed when a vaguely worded [memorandum of understanding](https://www.cnn.com/2026/06/17/politics/us-iran-memo-annotated-intl-vis) collapsed.

And his options for changing the equation — risking the lives of hundreds of US troops in a ground war or recognizing Tehran’s control of the Strait of Hormuz — are so unpalatable that the phrase “no good options” has become a cliche.

“We are really in a fix,” said Lyle Goldstein, director of Asia Engagement at the US-based Defense Priorities think tank.

The costs of the Iran war are not confined to the participants. The political and economic backlash is mounting in the Middle East and Euro

## Insight Focus

Extreme heat is ravaging crops across Europe. But this is not the only supportive factor for commodities. Both the conflict in the Persian Gulf and Russia’s war on Ukraine are creating bullish headlines for grains, oilseeds and energy this month. Meanwhile, diplomatic relations are also adding uncertainty to global markets as new US tariffs come into force.

July has been fraught with tensions between the US and Israel. Despite a ceasefire and diplomatic talks, missile attacks resumed. At the beginning of July, reports emerged that Iranian forces fired missiles at commercial vessels in the Strait of Hormuz and a tanker was struck near Oman, causing the price of oil to spike from just over USD 70/bbl to over USD 100/bbl.

# Russian port restrictions threaten Egyptian wheat supply chains

Egypt’s wheat supply chain is facing fresh disruption after Russia restricted truck deliveries at three Black Sea terminals that supply the country’s grain, as escalating drone attacks threaten regional shipping routes, *[Reuters](https://www.reuters.com/world/three-russian-black-sea-terminals-restrict-grain-intake-by-truck-amid-shipping-2026-07-28/)* reported, citing five grain industry sources.

The affected facilities — the NZT and KSK terminals in Novorossiysk and the ZTKT terminal in Taman — together handle more than 20 million tons of grain a year, over 40% of Russia’s total seaborne grain exports, and serve major buyers including Egypt and Turkey.

Port-level figures indicate the scale of Egypt-bound wheat traffic passing through the affected terminals. [Novorossiysk](https://portnews.ru/news/388999/) port shipped 1.5 million tons of wheat to Egypt in January and February 2026, while [Taman](https://www.kommersant.ru/doc/8463081) shipped 29,300 tons between Jan. 1 and Feb. 26. Together, the affected terminals in both ports supplied about 1.53 million tons within two months, equivalent to roughly 12% of [Egypt’s annual import requirement](https://www.fas.usda.gov/data

# BARONE: Ukrainian war remakes war

## 

##### By Michael Barone - | Jul 30, 2026

![](https://ogden_images.s3.amazonaws.com/www.heraldextra.com/images/2021/08/02064102/61e31600773e3596f5bebeaba546a91b-331x500.jpg)

Michael Barone

Wars remake war. New weaponry, new tactics, new strategy time and again produce results no one predicted or thought possible.

Revolutionary France’s levee en masse and Napoleon’s bold attacks prevailed over staid 18th-century siege warfare and subdued all Europe. The aggressive assaults produced horrendous casualties but were unable to move the Western Front trenches more than a few meters in World War I.

Less than 20 years later, the European theater in World War II was the scene of blitzkrieg attacks — France, with Europe’s largest army, was overrun in six weeks — followed by the heavily mechanized Allied forces moving forward as fast as logistics permitted.

The war in Ukraine seems to be remaking war once again. When Vladimir Putin ordered Russian troops to march into Kyiv in February 2022, he expected they’d be welcomed, and U.S. intelligence assumed they’d encounter no serious resistance and called for evacuation.
